body_ar:
ما هي وسائل زيادة الإيمان?

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين، أما بعد فإن هذا الإيمان هو الذي يميز أهل السعادة عن أهل الشقاء، وهو الذي يختار الله له من يميزهم ويهيئهم لمرضاته ولدخول جناته، والإنسان محتاج إلى تعاهده دائما لأنه يبلى ويجد في النفوس.

فهو الذي يحمل على الطاعات ويحمل على ترك المعاصي، ونحن محتاجون إليه حاجة شديدة لا تعدلها حاجة إلى أي شيء آخر، فلذلك لا بد من تذاكر زيادته ونقصه وأسباب ذلك دائما، فالإيمان نطق باللسان واعتقاد بالجنان وعمل بالأركان يزيد بالطاعات وينقص بالعصيان، فهو اعتقاد بالجنان أي بالقلب، ونطق باللسان بتصديق ذلك، وعمل بالأركان أي بالجوارح بالامتثال والاجتناب،
body_en:
What are the means of increasing faith?

In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon the one who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his practice until the Day of Judgement. To proceed: this faith (īmān) is what marks off the people of felicity from the people of wretchedness. It is that for which God chooses those whom He marks off and makes ready for His good pleasure and for entry into His gardens. A person needs to tend to it constantly, because within souls it wears out and is made new again.

It is faith that carries a person to acts of obedience and carries him to leaving off acts of disobedience. Our need of it is so intense that no need of anything else is its equal. For that reason there must be constant reminding of one another about its increase and its decrease and the causes of these. Faith is utterance with the tongue, belief with the heart, and action with the limbs; it increases with acts of obedience and decreases with disobedience. So it is belief with the janān — that is, with the heart; and utterance with the tongue, affirming that; and action with the arkān — that is, with the bodily members, by compliance and by avoidance,

flags.context: the reason given for needing to tend to faith constantly
options: because within souls it wears out and is made new again
because it wears out and finds a place within souls
because it wears thin and is renewed in the soul
flags.note: The consonantal يجد can be read yajidd ('becomes new', from jadda) or yajid ('finds'). The first reading is almost certainly right, because the Sheikh is drawing on the well-known report that faith wears out in the breast as a garment wears out and must be renewed — which is also why he pairs it with yablā, 'wears out'. The source is unvowelled and he does not quote the report here, so the reading is flagged rather than fixed.

flags.arabic: فالإيمان نطق باللسان واعتقاد بالجنان وعمل بالأركان يزيد بالطاعات وينقص بالعصيان
flags.context: the definition of faith the Sheikh gives
options: render as plain prose, keeping janān and arkān where he glosses them himself
render as prose and drop the Arabic terms, since he glosses them
flags.note: This is a rhymed mnemonic formula (al-lisān / al-janān / al-arkān / al-ṭāʿāt / al-ʿiṣyān) of the kind memorised in the mahdara. The rhyme has not been reproduced, per the house rule against rhymed English. The two Arabic words have been kept in the English only in the second, explanatory sentence, where the Sheikh himself glosses them, because dropping them there would make his gloss read as a tautology.

flags.context: وعمل بالأركان أي بالجوارح بالامتثال والاجتناب،
options: end the English on the comma exactly as the Arabic ends
mark the break with an ellipsis
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The published page breaks off mid-clause, on a comma, with the full lecture behind the .docx download. The English ends on the same comma. Note that the title promises 'the means of increasing faith' and the excerpt stops before a single such means is named — the reader is given the definition of faith and nothing of what the title offers.

Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The opening is the khuṭbat al-ḥājah, the standard formula with which the Sheikh begins a lecture. It is rendered in full rather than abbreviated, since it is part of the text as published.

EXCERPT ONLY. The page publishes the opening of the lecture and breaks off; the full text sits behind the .docx download recorded in source_download_link. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and the thought has not been completed. The site must render this with an excerpt banner and never as a whole article.
The question mark at the end of the question in the source is the Latin '?' rather than the Arabic '؟'; preserved in body_ar.
'The people of felicity' and 'the people of wretchedness' render ahl al-saʿādah and ahl al-shaqāʾ, the standard eschatological pair.
